stage_a.note: Founder smiles, is highly engaged, and maintains a confident, positive tone.
Founder energetically introduces the game and its premise with clear excitement.
Friendly and conversational delivery, addressing the panel warmly.

venture.description: A physical board game parodying internet culture where players compete to gain the most social media followers.
venture.note: The founder introduces the specific board game Influencers in the Wild.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Presents the board game Influencers in the Wild, explaining the premise of gaining followers instead of money.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks the founder to demonstrate how the board game is played.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Echoes the request to see how the game is actually played.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees to show the game, dismisses the model from the stage, and introduces her as an influencer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Inquires about the number of followers the model has on social media.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Endorses the founder, stating he is a genuine and popular figure on social media.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Expresses appreciation for the investor's endorsement.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks the founder to explain his own social media presence since she is unfamiliar with him.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Clarifies that the investor actually does follow his specific good news account.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Realizes she knows the founder's account and acknowledges it enthusiastically.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms the account name and her followership.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Adds that he also follows the account and praises the positive content.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Shares his long-time fandom of the show and credits it for his business education.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Prompts the founder to return to the business pitch.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Re-asks for an explanation of the game's rules.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains the board game mechanics, focusing on landing on blue spaces and drawing cards.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Notes the blue playing cards as part of the game setup.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Reads a game card aloud about using photos on a dating app to gain followers.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains that the winner is determined by tallying followers at the end.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Confirms that the player with the most followers wins.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees with the investor's understanding of the winning condition.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Expresses enjoyment of the game while holding up a card about being verified.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks the founder about his personal background and how he started the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Details his interests and explains he created a physical product to avoid relying solely on social media algorithms.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Requests details about the business side and retail progress.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States they recently secured an exclusive deal with a major big box retailer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Questions how retail customers will understand the product and be motivated to purchase it.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Compares the game to similar successful titles and discusses unexpected demographic data from their retail placement.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks for the total number of units sold.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Reports that they have sold around fifteen hundred units so far.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Criticizes the sales figure as being very poor.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Concedes that the sales numbers are indeed bad.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks how many retail stores the game was placed in.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States the game was in nineteen hundred stores and agrees the performance is poor.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Points out that the sales volume is insufficient.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Warns that the product will be delisted for not generating enough margin for the retailer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Acknowledges the risk but defends the margins, noting the product has only been in stores for two months.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Demands the specific financial numbers for the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Provides the manufacturing costs, which vary based on order volume.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks for the wholesale price of the game.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Details the retail price, the wholesale price through a broker, and the broker's margin.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Comments that the margin sounds reasonable.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Inquires about the volume of direct-to-consumer sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Admits they have not generated any direct-to-consumer sales yet.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks for the total dollar amount of product sold.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States the broker has sold a specific dollar amount and expresses confidence in future sales.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Challenges the valuation, asking for justification beyond the current sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Admits that the valuation is not based on real numbers and was essentially made up.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Criticizes the founder for choosing an unrealistic valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jokingly roleplays an investor rejecting the pitch due to the absurd numbers.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Exits, citing the difficulty of the toy industry and the unjustifiable valuation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Asks the exiting investor why he believes the company is not worth the requested valuation.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Interjects that the company is not currently generating profit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Concedes that the company is not yet profitable.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Points out that investing based solely on future potential is a significant ask.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Notes the uncertainty of the game's appeal and suggests a lower ask would have been acceptable.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains that a smaller ask would not cover the inventory costs required for a major retail order.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Explains the high sales volume required to return the requested investment amount.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Acknowledges the investors' need for a return on their capital.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Emphasizes that investors expect a multiple on their money, reiterating that the ask was too high.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees with the investor's assessment of the deal structure mistake.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Exits, feeling the risk is too high given the uncertainty of consumer reception.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Attempts to offer a different perspective on the company's valuation.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Exits, stating the valuation is too high compared to acquiring other game developers outright.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Exits, praising the founder's wit but refusing to risk money on such low sales figures.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Thanks the panel as the pitch concludes.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Suggests the founder put her endorsement on the game's packaging.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Advises the founder to add stickers with his social media handles to the boxes to drive sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jokingly asks if adding the endorsements means they have a deal.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Laughs and tells the founder he has a better chance with that strategy.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Wishes the founder luck as he leaves the tank.

decisions.note: Toy industry is too hard, most submissions fail, valuation is crazy, won't write a $500k check.
Unsure if people will enjoy the game, $500k is too much money to risk on it.
For $500k he could acquire 70-90% of an undiscovered game, valuation is too rich.
Asking too much money for only 1500 units sold, it's taking too big of a chance.
End of pitch, wishes him luck without making an offer, implied exit.

record.notes: Implied exit for S2 at the end of the pitch based on his sign-off 'Good luck man'.
